papers.title: The sharp uniqueness threshold for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on regular trees
papers.abstract: We study Gibbs uniqueness for the $q$-state antiferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite rooted $d$-ary tree and the infinite $(d+1)$-regular tree, where $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. An edge has weight $p\in[0,1]$ if its endpoints have the same color and weight $1$ otherwise. We prove that there is a unique Gibbs state if and only if $p\geqslant p_c:=\max\{0,1-q/(d+1)\}$, except when $(q,p)=(d+1,0)$, thus completes the uniqueness thresholds for all $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. Our proof use a convex potential for the tree recursion and show that it strictly decreases away from the uniform distribution. Together with the result of Gu, Wu and Yang, our theorem gives the exact critical power law whenever $p_c>0$.

papers.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
papers.abstract: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(\alpha\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(\alpha\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.

papers.title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $\Gamma$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.

papers.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
papers.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

papers.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow
papers.abstract: Viscoelastic flow past two side-by-side microcylinders has been shown to exhibit geometry-dependent transitions among symmetric, converging, diverging, and asymmetric-diverging flow states, together with regions of bistability and tristability. Here, we develop a data-driven framework for learning a two-dimensional, parameter-dependent normal form for this bifurcation structure from sparse measurements of stable flow states. We use the flow asymmetry parameters $I'$ and $I''$ as state variables, with the gap ratio $G$ and Weissenberg number $Wi$ as control parameters. In the absence of trajectory data, the measured steady states are enforced as stable equilibria of the learned vector field through equilibrium and local-stability constraints. We examine both polynomial and neural-network representations of the associated normal form and incorporate the physical reflection symmetry directly into the model. The resulting models recover the main geometry-dependent transitions and the overall structure of the experimental phase diagram. To reduce additional stable equilibria that are not constrained by the measurements, we introduce an iterative negative-sample procedure that refines the predicted equilibrium structure. Combining equilibrium data, local stability, physical symmetry, and negative samples yields the closest agreement with the experimental phase diagram among the models considered. The remaining discrepancies reflect the limited information available, solely in the form of sparse equilibrium measurements. Overall, the framework aims to showcase a prototypical example of both the potential and the limitations of inferring nonlinear flow dynamics from sparse equilibrium measurements and highlight the importance of physical constraints and additional dynamical information for reconstructing complex bifurcation structures.

papers.title: Defining the mathematical family tree with a minimal programming language
papers.abstract: I introduce MLISP, a Turing-complete language with nine single-character commands (a b c d f 0 i j k), and use it to define 88 mathematical structures and a family tree of 65 theories that they model, with three aims: Pedagogy: It presents the mathematical structures in a unified way, with standardized presentation tableaus that define them and axiomatized theories that describe them. Connections: It highlights how they are related in the family tree via added symbols, axioms, etc. While the full tree is obviously infinite, its lower parts naturally separate into six main branches: the relational branch, the algebraic branch, the logic branch, the number branch, the set branch and the continuum branch. Foundations: The definitions, key theorems and models of each entry are verified in Lean. Mathematical structures are defined as equivalence classes of presentations, which in a constructivist spirit are defined in a simple, explicit and self-contained way in standardized presentation tableaus with minimal human baggage. For finite structures, the generating functions are defined by lookup tables. For countably infinite ones, they are instead defined computationally using MLISP, since more complex languages such as Lean are massive overkill for rigorously defining standard arithmetic operations (for example, the program "jibjbfid" defines subtraction). An interactive version is available at https://tegmark.org/mathtree. The Lean code is public, also verifies the correctness of MLISP and includes 43% of the theorems from Mathlib 2026-10-11. \end{abstract}

papers.title: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--B\'enard convection
papers.abstract: We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--B\'enard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0<\sigma\leq1$ in the temperature equation. For every deterministic initial temperature, we prove that \[ \underline{Nu}-1 \geq c(\sigma^3 Ra)^{7/192}, \] provided that \[ \sigma^3 Ra \geq C(1+\log(1/\sigma))^{192/7}, \] where $c,C>0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional It\^o process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.

papers.title: Extended group analysis and conservation laws of a class of variable coefficient generalized Kawahara equations
papers.abstract: We review and extend the results on the group analysis of a class of generalized Kawahara equations with time-dependent coefficients. First, we provide an overview of the existing literature on Lie symmetries and Lie-invariant solutions of such equations. We then present a complete description of their transformation properties, including admissible, equivalence, and Lie symmetry transformations. For practical applications, we further extend these results by presenting a complete Lie symmetry classification without simplifying the coefficients via equivalence transformations. Lie reductions are then systematically performed, and several exact solutions are constructed. Low-order local conservation laws are exhaustively classified: every equation in this class admits conservation of mass and the squared $L^2$ norm, whereas energy-type conservation laws exist only for specific coefficient branches that align with the cases singled out by the symmetry classification. Finally, the classification results are enhanced by a study of contractions, which link cases of Lie symmetry extensions together with the associated reductions and conservation laws.

papers.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
papers.abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.

papers.title: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, with $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.

papers.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
papers.abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

papers.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

papers.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperk\"ahler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

papers.title: Noncommutative $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed beta functions of first and second kind : beta gamma relations, shift identities and symmetrisation
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $\phi_{1}>\phi_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominus\phi_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplus\phi_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $\phi_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all complex arguments with positive real parts; we derive its general shift identity, its exchange defect $\phi_{1}^{(y-x)(x+y-1)/2}$, a commutative symmetrisation unique up to a constant, its asymptotics and a deformed Euler integral for a deformed Gauss hypergeometric function, which yields a deformed Gauss summation. The second kind function is evaluated through Ramanujan's ${}_{1}\psi_{1}$ summation and involves a second deformed gamma function, differing from the first one by a one periodic theta quotient, so that its exchange defect persists in the one parameter case. We prove a Bohr Mollerup type characterisation and a multiplication formula for the deformed gamma function, show that it is logarithmically convex on the positive half line if and only if $\phi_{1}\geq1$, obtain the joint logarithmic convexity of normalised beta functions with a deformed Tur\'an identity, and compute the moments of the associated deformed beta distributions. Gauge invariance covers the Jagannathan Srinivasa Rao, Chakrabarti Jagannathan, generalized $q-$Quesne and Hounkonnou Ngompe deformations, and every identity is confirmed numerically to thirty digits.

papers.title: Uniformly positive correlations in the dimer model and phase transition in lattice permutations on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d > 2$, via reflection positivity
papers.abstract: Our first main result is that correlations between monomers in the dimer model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ do not decay to zero when $d > 2$. This is the first rigorous result about correlations in the dimer model in dimensions greater than two and shows that the model behaves drastically differently than in two dimensions, in which case it is integrable and correlations are known to decay to zero polynomially. Such a result is implied by our more general, second main result, which states the occurrence of a phase transition in the model of lattice permutations, which is related to the quantum Bose gas. More precisely, we consider a self-avoiding walk interacting with lattice permutations and we prove that, in the regime of fully-packed loops, such a walk is `long' and the distance between its end-points grows linearly with the diameter of the box. These results follow from the derivation of a version of the infrared bound from a new general probabilistic settings, with coloured loops and walks interacting at sites and walks entering into the system from some `virtual' vertices. In dimension $d=3$ we use a transfer matrix argument to obtain a sharper infrared bound.

papers.title: Dubrovin duality for open Hurwitz flat F-manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dubrovin dual of a Hurwitz Frobenius manifold extends naturally to an F-manifold with compatible flat connection on the universal curve, in the sense of the open WDVV equations. A similar result is proven for the Frobenius manifold itself in arXiv:2503.09258 . This equips the universal curve with two F-manifolds with compatible flat structure, and we study their duality. We show that they combine into a bi-flat F-manifold. Conditions on open WDVV solutions imposed in previous work are retrieved in this setting, thus providing them with a geometrical meaning. Finally, explicit examples are computed. For Saito Frobenius manifolds of types $A$ and $D$, the extended prepotentials coincide with open WDVV solutions computed independently, whereas even the existence of the solution in type $E$ had not been previously discussed. On the other hand, new non-homogeneous solutions are constructed by duality.

papers.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.

papers.title: Interface Invariants of Rhombohedral Graphene with Layer-dependent Potentials and Couplings
papers.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

papers.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
papers.abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.

papers.title: Cantor spectrum at a fixed Diophantine frequency
papers.abstract: We establish that the spectrum of one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrodinger operators exhibits Cantor structure in the regime of positive Lyapunov exponents for every fixed Diophantine frequency. The proof follows the general strategy of the gap construction by Goldstein and the second author, but avoids the elimination of double and triple resonances used in the original argument. A novel ingredient is the use of Holder continuity of the integrated density of states (IDS) to exclude energies at which eigenvalue parametrizations in finite volume have small slopes. We also use a linear bound in the volume on the number of zeros of Dirichlet determinants, and a pigeonholing argument to obtain lower bounds on the distances between eigenvalues. The crossing of two translated Rellich functions with opposite slopes produces a local maximum whose eigenfunctions have exponentially small boundary values. Together with finite volume eigenvalue separation, this forces the DOS mass to concentrate near the maximum. However, on an interval of constancy of the acceleration, the Lyapunov exponent is analytic, and hence the DOS is Lipschitz there. This ultimately leads to a contradiction near the maximum.

papers.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
papers.abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

papers.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
papers.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $\beta_f^-(q)=\beta_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-\nu_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $\nu_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.

papers.title: The polarization bundle of a bending ray: nested projections and helicity Chern numbers
papers.abstract: We consider a ray propagating in a weakly anisotropic, possibly absorbing medium. The transverse planes of the propagation directions form a rank-two complex vector bundle $E_\perp$ over the sphere $S^2$ of directions. The polarization states are the points of $Z=\mathbb{CP}(E_\perp)$. Projecting the flat derivative of $\mathbb{C}^3$ onto $E_\perp$ gives a connection $D$, the complexified Levi-Civita connection of $S^2$, whose holonomy is the Rytov rotation. Projecting $D$ onto a polarization line gives the connection of the tautological line bundle over $Z$, whose holonomy is the Pancharatnam--Berry phase. For the horizontal distribution defined by $D$, the curvature of this bundle is $i\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the vertical part, $i s_3\,\omega$ on the horizontal part, and zero on the mixed part. Here $\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the Fubini--Study form, $\omega$ the area form of $S^2$, and $s_3$ the circular Stokes parameter. The Rytov rotation, the Pancharatnam--Berry phase and the Chern numbers $c_1(L_\pm)=\mp 2$ are all obtained from this curvature. Restricted to the helicity sections, it gives the obstruction to a globally smooth circular Jones vector, although the circular polarization states are globally defined.

papers.title: Compressional-shear wave interference and wave suppression at exceptional-point gaps
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in complex elastic materials signify the coalescence of compressional and shear modes and bound a frequency gap where waves become evanescent. While their effects on wave propagation have been extensively studied, the physical mechanisms underlying their existence remain elusive. In this Letter, employing a transfer matrix formulation combined with Bloch's theorem, we demonstrate that the gaps bounded by EPs in layered media originate from destructive interference between the compressional and shear wave fields. We further reveal that the corresponding wavenumbers satisfy a Bragg-like condition with the unit cell thickness, causing the total wave field to become stationary, forming a standing wave. Finally, a finite layered medium is considered, where this mechanism is shown to manifest as forbidden wave propagation for both modes in the gap. These results provide a direct physical interpretation of EPs.

papers.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
papers.abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

papers.title: On Lipschitz equicontinuity of random Schr\"odinger operators on lattices
papers.abstract: We consider random Schr\"odinger operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We prove that the density of states is uniformly bounded in the coupling strength for a dense set of single site probability distributions.

papers.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
papers.abstract: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2\omega^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.

papers.title: Quantum Landau Damping with Coulomb Repulsion in the Whole Space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the large time behavior of solutions to the linearized Hartree equation near a stable equilibrium which is homogeneous in space and investigate the quantum Landau damping. This allows us to get time decay of the electric field, uniformly in the Planck constant, as well as the uniform-in-time convergence of the quantum density towards the classical density as the Planck constant converges to 0.

papers.title: Obstructions to Hadamard Deformations of Fourier Matrices
papers.abstract: We study deformations of the Fourier spin model commuting square in the space of commuting squares, or equivalently deformations of the matrix $\sqrt nF_n$, where $F_n$ denotes the Fourier matrix, by complex Hadamard matrices. If $n$ is neither a prime power nor twice a prime, we show that there exist unit vectors in the enveloping tangent space that cannot be realized as directions of convergence of sequential deformations. Consequently, the derivative of any differentiable Hadamard family through $\sqrt nF_n$ has rank strictly smaller than the dimension of the enveloping tangent space at $\sqrt nF_n$ (i.e., the defect of $F_n$). This is particularly surprising because for every $n$ there exist enough one-parameter analytic families to provide a basis of directions in the enveloping tangent space. We obtain cubic obstructions when $n$ has at least three distinct prime divisors, quartic obstructions when it has exactly two and a repeated factor, and quintic obstructions when it is the product of two distinct odd primes. These results extend our order $30$ result from \cite{HN}.

papers.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
papers.abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.
